subject: Renewal: EU residency + APAC on-ramp and cross-region failover
messages:

Subject: Renewal: EU residency + APAC on‑ramp

Hi Aditya,

We're coming up on our renewal for EuroHealth (contract EH-4392) and legal/ops have two things they want to be reflected in the new term:

1) EU data residency: all patient-derived embeddings and request logs must remain in the EU (Germany).
2) APAC on‑ramp: we want a controlled rollout to APAC (Singapore + Japan) to support our pilot in Q4 — ideally with cross-region failover back to EU for continuity.

Can Redwood provide a single SOW that covers the EU residency guarantee, the APAC on‑ramp (timeline & capacity), and a short description of the failover behaviour and encryption/KMS approach? Our procurement target is to finalize financials and legal redlines by mid‑June so we can sign before quarter end.

Thanks — can we do a 30min sync next week?

Best,
Katrin Müller
Head of Platform Ops
EuroHealth Systems

Subject: RE: Renewal: EU residency + APAC on‑ramp

Hi Katrin — following our call today, summarising the ops and SOW options so legal has concrete text to review: 

Option A — EU-primary (lower cost)
- All inference and logs for EuroHealth account are stored and processed in our EU region (Frankfurt/DE).
- APAC users are routed to EU for inference; we can provide a read-through KV cache in SG to reduce latency but no long‑term storage in APAC.
- Failover: if EU region is unavailable, traffic will be routed to a warm standby in APAC but logs/outputs will be written to EU once connectivity resumes.
- KMS: Redwood-managed KMS by default; customer‑managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) available as an add‑on.
- Pricing delta for read-through cache / burst capacity: +18% on current per‑token rate.

Option B — Dedicated APAC capacity (higher availability, higher cost)
- Dedicated GPU pool in APAC under a committed capacity SKU. All APAC inference stays in APAC.
- Cross‑region failover mechanics: traffic prefers local APAC; if APAC capacity exhausted or region degraded, traffic fails over to EU with controlled routing and explicit preservation of EU‑only storage flags.
- KMS: BYOK with HSM integration available; encryption at rest in each region.
- Pricing: committed monthly model; estimated uplift ~+42% relative to current spend (depends on commit).

SOW next steps: we attached SOW v2 with explicit redline language for the residency clause and the failover SLAs. If legal confirms the residency phrase ("Personal data and embeddings SHALL be stored and processed only in European Union territories unless explicitly authorized in writing by Customer"), we can produce an amendment and DocuSign envelope aimed at June 15 signature.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise\Redwood Inference

Thanks for the summary and the SOW v2 — that helps. A couple of items from legal/security: 

- The residency sentence you proposed is close; legal insists on explicit non-replication to outside EU for "patient-derived embeddings" and an audit clause allowing EuroHealth to request export logs quarterly.
- Can you provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a short diagram of the keyflow for BYOK/HSM (our security team wants to see key custody and rotation words).
- There will be a small contract redline to the SLA section (availability credits and failover time objective). We will send redlines back in DocuSign-ready format by end of day Monday.

Timelines: we need countersigned contracts by June 22 to align procurement approvals. Is the June 15 sign target still feasible if we accept Option B (dedicated APAC) but with a 12‑month committed term and the residency clause locked to EU for analytics/logs?

I'll copy our APAC pilot lead Satoshi for schedule coordination.

Regards,
Katrin

1) SOW + Amendment: Attached is the final SOW (v3) with the residency clause adjusted per legal's wording: "Personal data and embeddings arising from EuroHealth customer workloads SHALL be stored and processed solely within EU territories unless Customer provides explicit written authorization for specific artifacts to be replicated to APAC for latency reasons." Please review the redline in the attached PDF.

2) Security evidence: We've bundled SOC2 Type II summary and a keyflow diagram in security-evidence.zip. BYOK/HSM flow shown: customer master key (CMK) in your KMS -> attested HSM -> per-region data keys encrypted with CMK. Rotation policies included.

3) Pricing & commit: Rishi has produced two commercial options in the SOW: (A) EU-primary + APAC read-through cache (12% uplift), (B) Dedicated APAC committed pool with 12‑month commit (40% uplift). See pages 6-7 of the SOW for line-item pricing.

4) DocuSign: I created the DocuSign envelope for Amendment + SOW: https://redwood.example/docusign/EH-4392-renewal. If we get countersignature by June 15 we can lock the APAC capacity and schedule onboarding for late July.

Next actions:
- Katrin: confirm whether EuroHealth will accept the residency language above, and which pricing option (A or B) you prefer.
- Satoshi: please confirm the pilot RPS numbers and preferred SG/JP region start dates.
- Marissa: coordinate the onboarding checklist and share the training window availability for July.

We'll prepare the final amendment doc for legal review once Katrin confirms.
